extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in 19th-century exploration, natural history, and travel/narrative accounts (also useful to sailors and colonial administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Compose a first-person travel/exploration narrative that combines personal adventure, natural-history observation, nautical detail, and moral/social reflection for a general readership. The form interleaves precise measurements and scientific notes with dramatic anecdotes and ethnographic comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise empirical/geographical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of exact positions, measurements and nautical data (e.g., "placed Point Pearce in latitude 14 degrees 25 minutes 50 seconds, South longitude 2 degrees 49 minutes West of Port Essington"; tide times; soundings in fathoms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide coordinates, tide times, depths (fathoms), soundings and other quantitative observations to lend scientific credibility and utility to the narrative; these details are interleaved with the story (examples: times of high-water, bank positions, depths from 30 to 60 fathoms, specific lat/longs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine narrative with scientific/natural-history observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermix personal adventure with natural-history notes and species records (e.g., observations of new species, the silk cotton-tree, 'gouty-stem tree', kangaroo species, tortoise, fish, birds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance evocative narrative passages with cataloguing and description of flora, fauna and geological features; include specimens, species names, and references to figures/plates to support the natural-history element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicious restraint about distressing detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit choice to avoid over-describing suffering ("The sufferings of that night I will not fatigue my readers by describing").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know when to withhold graphic detail for the reader's sake; imply intensity without prolonged, sensational narration when appropriate for tone and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid, suspenseful action scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediate, present-tense-feeling description of danger and escape (e.g., the spearing: 'I was suddenly staggered by a violent and piercing blow... a loud long yell... told me by whom I had been speared').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, kinetic sentences, sensory detail (blow, yell, pursuit), and pacing that conveys urgency; include concrete gestures and short clauses to maintain tension in episodes of peril.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and social reflection woven into report
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorial moral commentary on treatment of indigenous people and colonial policy ("Surely this reflection should now and then present itself to the white man ... induce him to judge more leniently").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interleave descriptive reportage with ethical observations and appeals to reader sympathy or reform; use reflective passages to contextualize encounters and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrations, figures and footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to annexed woodcuts and footnotes for species/visuals (e.g., footnote: 'Figured by Mr. Gould from this specimen as Amadina gouldiae.'; references to woodcuts annexed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support textual descriptions with plates/figures and explanatory footnotes for scientific names, pronunciations, provenance and cross-references; use notes to keep the main narrative flowing while providing technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of indigenous/local terminology with glosses
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide native names and their correspondences (table: settler name, native name, genus, remarks; e.g., 'Mahogany : Jarrail : Eucalyptus').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record indigenous toponyms and vernacular plant/animal names, offer transliterations/pronunciation notes, and explain local usage to enrich ethnographic accuracy and cultural detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter outlining and signposting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of chapter headings and content lists to preview subjects (e.g., 'CHAPTER 2.4. VICTORIA RIVER TO SWAN RIVER.' followed by an enumerated list of topics to be treated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orient the reader with a clear chapter title and a concise list or summary of forthcoming items to structure long exploratory narratives and set reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix of technical nautical register and lyrical description
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternation between precise nautical terms (helm, tack, soundings, fathoms) and evocative, poetic passages (sunset described as 'a stream of fire over the water').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the appropriate register for the material: use technical language when reporting navigational/operational facts; shift to lyrical prose for landscape, mood, and human emotion to produce stylistic contrast and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-person observer voice for credibility and intimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Narration in first person as eyewitness ('I had just turned my head... I was suddenly staggered... I was soon got down to the boat...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present events through the narrator's direct perspective to lend immediacy and authority; combine subjective impressions with verifiable facts to balance personal involvement and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toponymic naming as narrative device and record
rubrics_metrics.description: Naming places to commemorate events ("To commemorate the accident which befell me, the bay within Point Pearce was called Treachery Bay, and a high hill over it Providence Hill").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use place-naming to mark significant incidents, create memorable geography, and record human interactions with landscape; explain names' origins for historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of corroborating eyewitness accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding other witnesses' narratives within the main account (e.g., 'Lieutenant Roe's account of his rescuing Captain Grey's party' and Roe's first-hand narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment the narrator's perspective with other eyewitness testimonies to broaden viewpoint, add credibility and vary narrative voice; clearly attribute and contextualize these inserted accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative/seasonal observation to infer patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparing conditions across times/places to draw inferences (e.g., observations that parts of rivers are 'perfectly dry' though 'last year those very parts were running with a good stream').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record repeated or contrasting observations over time and across locations to note seasonal variability or long-term tendencies; use comparative statements to support hypotheses about hydrology, climate, or ecology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethological/behavioral observation of local peoples
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording indigenous behaviors and customs with specific details (e.g., 'The natives never throw a spear when the eye of the person they aim at is turned towards them'; skill in tracking 'tell Mr. Roe ... THE NAME OF EACH').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note specific observed behaviors, hunting/war conventions, tracking skill and social reactions; present such observations carefully and contextualize to avoid overgeneralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical navigational and safety advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing actionable guidance for seafarers (e.g., 'Ships, therefore, passing along the North-west coast ... should be prepared for bad weather.'; 'proper berth... in seven or eight fathoms... about a mile from the gaol').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include practical recommendations based on experience—anchorages, likely winds, storm-season timing, safe berths and hazards—so the narrative can serve as a useful manual for mariners.
